one_liner: Fixed-capacity char-array type with SIMD-accelerated equality, compare, and fixed-width integer/string conversion, beating std::string and stoi/to_string in author benchmarks.
what_it_does: Str<SIZE> is a template-parameterized, fixed-length char array wrapper (single header, Str.h) offering equality, three-way compare, and fixed-width decimal integer conversion (toi/toi64/fromi) as member functions. It is not a resizable string: capacity is a compile-time template parameter, there is no append/substr/find, and instances behave like a POD raw byte array rather than a null-terminated C string. It pairs with a separate StrHash open-addressing table (out of scope here) for use as a fast map/hash key.
how_it_is_fast: operator==/compare fold the array into 8-byte word comparisons and use __builtin_ctzll to locate the first differing byte, avoiding a per-byte loop, and switch to AVX-512 (VL+BW) masked byte compares (_mm512/256/128_cmpneq_epu8_mask) when the target supports it. fromi/toi convert between fixed-width, zero-padded decimal digits and integers using a branchless SIMD digit-pair multiply-add trick (SSE4.1 pmaddubsw/pmaddwd chain, citing arXiv:1902.08318 Fig.7) for 8/16-digit chunks, plus a precomputed 2-character lookup table for the remaining/non-SIMD path, replacing libc's division-per-digit stoi/to_string loop.
when_to_use: Fixed-width string fields known at compile time (exchange/ticker symbols, FIX/ITCH-style protocol codes, instrument IDs)
Hot-path equality/ordering comparisons of short (up to tens of bytes), fixed-length keys, e.g. market-data order-book keys
Fixed-width, zero-padded decimal integer<->string conversion where the exact digit width is known ahead of time (e.g. date/session codes)
x86-64 targets that can build with -march=native or at least enable SSE4.1/AVX-512 to hit the accelerated code paths
Low-latency code already avoiding heap allocation that wants a trivially-copyable POD string type usable as a map/hash key
when_not_to_use: Variable-length or arbitrary strings: Str has no resize/append/growth, its capacity is baked into the template parameter
General integer parsing/formatting: fromi/toi require the number to fit exactly in SIZE zero-padded digits; no sign handling or variable width like stoi/to_string
Non-x86 targets: Str.h includes <x86intrin.h> unconditionally, so it will not compile on ARM/aarch64
Constructing Str from a C-string/buffer shorter than SIZE: the (const char*) constructor does a raw SIZE-byte struct copy and can read past the source buffer
Projects wanting upstream support: last commit 2021-07-04, single maintainer, 127 stars, no CI beyond the bundled benchmarks

integration.min_toolchain: C++11 minimum; C++17 only needed for tosv() (std::string_view). Benchmarks build with g++ -march=native -O3 (benchfindstr/benchfindint additionally add -std=c++17); GCC version not stated.
integration.platforms: x86-64 only (unconditionally includes <x86intrin.h>); AVX-512VL+AVX-512BW enable the SIMD compare path, SSE4.1 enables the SIMD toi/fromi path, otherwise a generic 8-byte-word fallback is used
integration.thread_safety: not documented; Str itself is a stateless/POD char-array wrapper with no shared mutable state, so independent instances can be used concurrently, but this is not asserted anywhere in the docs

gotchas: Str(const char*) does a raw SIZE-byte struct copy (`*(const Str<SIZE>*)p`), which can read past the source buffer if it is shorter than SIZE — no null-termination or bounds checks

fromi/toi require the value to fit exactly in SIZE zero-padded decimal digits (no sign, no variable width); correctness is only exercised via asserts in the author's own benchmark, not enforced by the header

Which code path (and therefore the speedup) you get is decided at compile time by preprocessor macros (__AVX512VL__/__AVX512BW__/__SSE4_1__), so build flags like -march=native directly determine performance
AlignSize is documented but not enforced: Str is not required to be aligned, but the README/header notes that aligning it speeds up comparisons
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Str over to_static_string/FastString/fstring/buffet when the field width is a known compile-time constant (fixed-width protocol/exchange codes) and you want the fastest possible equality/compare plus fixed-width numeric conversion via word-at-a-time/AVX-512 compare and SIMD digit conversion; for general resizable strings or variable-width number formatting, use one of those siblings instead.
verified_claims_summary: Author's own bundled microbenchmarks (benchmark/benchcmp.cc for comparisons, benchmark/benchnum.cc for conversions; built with g++ -march=native -O3, no compiler version or hardware stated) report Str's operator==/compare running about 2x faster than strncmp/memcmp/std::string equivalents, and fromi/toi running about 10x faster than stoi/strtol/to_string/sprintf for fixed-width numeric conversions. The README gives only these round numbers, with no result tables.
status_note: Abandoned since 2021-07-04 (last commit), single maintainer, 127 stars, 2 open issues and no CI; MIT-licensed and small enough (single header) to vendor and freeze as-is.
